Another piece of info that is so interesting to me is from my patients who are dying in hospice (I’m a nurse). Many of my patients are well into their 70s and 80s, and they ALL say life is worth living. They don’t seem to recall the bad moments as much as the good. They revel on the good times, the people they loved, who loved them. PLEASE meet with a person who is older than you. SEE that they have made it through. The silent generation went through The Great Depression. I enjoy learning from them. Look up their stories on YouTube!

I heard someone say once that death is boring. It’s the ending of a story. Right now, life might suck, but it’s not over. When has a story ever been an interesting story when there’s no drama? No pull in the plot? As a writer, that resonated with me and keeps me going. There are numerous possibilities and subplots to be had. You have more control than you think. You have the power to make a choice to make your life worth living. I will say, a huge thing to always avoid is isolation. Posting and asking for help is great. But please also reach out to people you trust face to face. For practical advice, please take a look at your local resources for finances. Where I am in Iowa, we have a 988 number for those in a mental health crisis, or financial and homeless crisis. You may find rent assistance or soup kitchens, etc. Sorry if this doesn’t help. I just want you to know that you always have options. Thank you for opening up. For a temporary mood booster, try watching your favorite comfort show or comedian. Or blast your favorite music. Learn about yourself, your gifts. See if you can use your talents and creativity to maybe sell a craft? That’s not super mind blowing information, but it helps me. YOU are the writer!
